title: Sandustry Automation Tips — Conveyors, Filters & Flow
description: Sandustry automation habits: belt layout, filters, launchers, and how to stop hand-carrying materials in Early Access.

paragraphs: Do not blueprint a megabase on day one. Automate whatever currently wastes the most clicks — usually horizontal transport, vertical lifts, or sorting mixed dig output.
Steam's feature list centers conveyors, launchers, filters, fluids, and later drones and deeper tech.
Leave spare tile width for a second belt before the first belt is full.
Separate dig face → buffer → refine → sink, even if the first version is tiny.
Put filters before merges, not after a clogged junction.
Keep power, heat, and fluid lines readable; pixel factories die to spaghetti you cannot diagnose.
Rebuild in slices: replace one segment, run it, then extend.
When sand, slag, and ore share one path, throughput looks fine until one material floods the line. Filtering early is usually cheaper than widening everything.
Treat a mystery pile at the junction as a design bug, not a dig problem.
Exact building unlock order, ratios, and drone behavior change during Early Access. Use this page for principles; verify numbers on the official wiki and patch notes.
Pair with the Beginner Guide and Slag & Processing when byproducts stall the line.

faq.q: Should I automate before expanding the dig?
faq.a: If you are hand-carrying more than you dig, yes. Expanding dig volume without logistics just creates a prettier backlog.
Steam markets drones among deeper and later tech. Early progress usually leans on conveyors, launchers, and filters first.
